_about: Answer-key repairs for the FoM bank, applied by tools/key_fixes.py after the extractors. Each entry names what the source said, what the lecture supports, and why. Written 2026-10-14 by the FoM class rep from the existing 'The key looks wrong' flags, which had been explaining the error without changing what the bank scored against.

b1-w2-new-q13-13.why: 07 - Nerves: Nissl bodies are stacks of (rough) endoplasmic reticulum.

b4-w13-meds2024-q15-15.why: The bank's own key text says IgG, and 04 - Adaptive Immunity gives circulation, extracellular space and ADCC to IgG (B). The letters of this question and the next were swapped.

b4-w13-meds2024-q16-16.why: The bank's own key text says IgA, and 04 - Adaptive Immunity places mucosal secretion and breast milk with IgA (D).

b4-w14-meds2024-q3-3.why: 09 - Introduction to Vaccines: conjugates are more immunogenic and, as non-live vaccines, no less safe.

b4-w15-new-q19-19.why: 03 - Important Fungal Infections: wide, irregular, sparsely septate hyphae on calcofluor white of BAL in a transplant recipient is mucormycosis.

b4-w15-new-q5-5.why: The bank's own rationale says all of the options are true, and 06 - Approach to Allergy supports A, C and D.

b4-w14-meds2024-q35-35.why: 05 - Approach to Public Health and Outbreak Investigation describes an intermittent source as repeated spikes from one on-off source, not a mix of continuous and propagated spread, so D is false.

b2-w5-new-q10-10.why: 02 - Introduction to Blood Pressure Regulation ties TPR to vessel diameter and lists blood volume as a separate determinant, so statement iv is unsupported and i, ii, iii (B) is the answer.

b1-w3-ra-q2-2.why: The keyed option read '47, XX&': the Y was lost in transcription. 07 - Chromosome Disorder Testing gives Klinefelter as 47,XXY. The key (B) is unchanged; the option text is repaired.

b3-wb-heme-q89.lead: The correct answer is C, D, H.
b3-wb-heme-q89.why: The stem asks for 3 antidotes and the source key listed only two, but its own explanation names PCC/Octaplex (H) as the most targeted warfarin antidote.

b4-w14-new-q2-2.lead: I – D (direct contact); II – A (airborne); III – B (vector); IV – C (common vehicle, the option lost in transcription).
b4-w14-new-q2-2.why: 01 - Transmission of Infectious Agents puts C. difficile under direct contact and botulism under common vehicle, so I and IV cannot share a letter.

b3-w11-new-q15-15.why: Reticulin fibres are a marrow finding, not a blood film finding (02 - Approach to Leukocytosis), so as worded the true set is A and B, and no option offers it.

b3-w12-new-q21-21.why: The keyed option says 2 cycles for unfavourable disease while the bank's own note says 4. The lecture notes give no cycle counts, so it can't be settled without the slides.

b4-w14-meds2024-q33-33.why: The question depends on an epidemic curve that is missing from the bank, and the text alone points to a different answer from the key.

b4-wb-ii-q62.why: The source rationale reads 'A and B are correct'; the B had been split off the key during extraction.

b3-wb-heme-q26.lead: The correct answer is A, C, D, F.
b3-wb-heme-q26.why: The workbook key gives A, C, D, F, so the question is now scored as a select-all instead of shown as a self-marked answer.

b2-w7-new-q15-15.stem: Which are essential components of a preventative health visit for older adults?
b2-w7-new-q15-15.lead: The correct answer is E. The periodic health encounter for older adults runs on ALBUS: Acute issues and safety, Labs and vitals, Book follow-up, Update profile, Screening. Acute issues (A) and screening (C) are both in it. The MoCA (B) is not: the lecture advises against screening asymptomatic older adults for cognitive impairment. A "basic overall risk assessment" (D) is not one of the ALBUS components.
b2-w7-new-q15-15.why: The bank asked which are essential components "except" and keyed E, "A and C", which its own explanation calls essential. 02 - Periodic Health Encounter for Older Adults puts acute issues (A) and screening (C) in ALBUS, so the stem now asks which are essential, matching the key. Reader report #210.
